incidents.title: Nadine Marcy Solonas inquest and Indigenous-support recommendation
incidents.care_setting: Police custody, paramedic assessment, emergency care and interfacility transfer
incidents.summary: A B.C. inquest reviewed the circumstances of Nadine Marcy Solonas’s death after police custody, paramedic assessment, emergency care in Quesnel and transfer to Vancouver. The jury recommended a 24-hour, on-call Indigenous support position for Indigenous people in RCMP custody who refuse treatment or mistrust first responders.
incidents.formal_process_status: Inquest completed; jury recommendation issued
incidents.institutional_response: The verdict records that the Independent Investigations Office found no police action or inaction contributed to the death.
incidents.formal_outcome: The inquest established the medical cause and circumstances of death and made a prevention recommendation. It did not make a finding of racism or legal responsibility.
unresolved_questions: Was a recommendation-specific RCMP response published?
Was the recommended support position created or evaluated?

incidents.title: Emergency-department assessment and resuscitation consent agreement
incidents.care_setting: Emergency department
incidents.summary: BCCNM approved a consent agreement after finding that an emergency-room nurse did not adequately assess or perform resuscitative measures for an Indigenous person found apparently pulseless and unresponsive in a vestibule, and did not meet documentation standards.
incidents.formal_process_status: Regulatory consent agreement approved January 25, 2023
incidents.institutional_response: BCCNM issued a public reprimand and specified suspension and education terms if the former registrant reapplies.
incidents.formal_outcome: A professional-regulator consent agreement; not a court judgment or a broader health-system finding.
unresolved_questions: No separate public institutional response or system-level follow-up was located in the bounded review.

incidents.title: Consent and Indigenous-heritage regulatory agreement
incidents.care_setting: Nursing care in a public setting
incidents.summary: BCCNM approved a consent agreement after finding that a nurse performed a religious ritual on a client without informed consent and without considering the client’s Indigenous heritage.
incidents.formal_process_status: Regulatory consent agreement approved September 23, 2022
incidents.institutional_response: BCCNM imposed a four-month suspension, a temporary practice restriction, mentorship and remedial education.
incidents.formal_outcome: A professional-regulator consent agreement; not a court judgment or a finding about an entire institution.

incidents.title: Trevor Dubois hospital death and ongoing reviews
incidents.care_setting: Inpatient hospital and protective services
incidents.summary: Saskatchewan Health Authority acknowledged that Trevor Dubois died after an encounter involving Protective Services Officers at Royal University Hospital. SHA said police and Coroners Service investigations, a Critical Incident review, an internal review and a third-party use-of-force review were underway.
incidents.formal_process_status: Multiple reviews and investigations announced; no final public finding located
incidents.institutional_response: SHA said it suspended the involved officer pending review and a related labour investigation and was engaging Saskatoon Tribal Council and the family. In July 2026, SHA said the separate external review of protective-services protocols remained underway while contracted protective services were expanded in several communities.
incidents.formal_outcome: No final public police, coroner, Critical Incident or use-of-force outcome was located in the bounded search.
unresolved_questions: What did the announced reviews conclude?
Did any recommendation or policy change result from the incident?
How will the separate provincewide security review report its findings?

incidents.title: Randy Lampreau inquest and custody-health recommendations
incidents.care_setting: Police custody, prisoner health monitoring and emergency response
incidents.summary: A B.C. inquest reviewed the death of Randy Lampreau, an Indigenous man, in a Kamloops RCMP cell. The jury recommended changes to prisoner-wellness checks, health-care staffing in the cellblock, an Indigenous liaison, a sobering centre and oversight of detention guards.
incidents.formal_process_status: Inquest completed; six prevention recommendations issued
incidents.institutional_response: The verdict records that the Independent Investigations Office found no evidence that police officers committed a criminal offence in relation to the death. Indigenous-led reporting later quoted the Province as saying it had no plans for a Kamloops sobering centre at that time.
incidents.formal_outcome: The jury classified the death as accidental and made prevention recommendations. An inquest is fact-finding, not fault-finding, and did not determine legal responsibility or make a finding of racism.
unresolved_questions: Which recommendations received formal responses from the RCMP, City of Kamloops, Province or Interior Health?
Were the recommended health-care staffing, Indigenous liaison, monitoring or sobering-centre measures implemented?

incidents.title: Lindsey Izony inquest and custody-health recommendations
incidents.care_setting: Police custody, emergency medical response and hospital care
incidents.summary: A B.C. inquest reviewed Lindsey Izony's death after she experienced a medical emergency in Prince George RCMP custody, was treated by paramedics and was transported to University Hospital of Northern B.C. Public Indigenous-focused research and community reporting identify Izony as a Tsek'ene woman. The jury made six prevention recommendations concerning First Nations substance-use services, detention-guard standards, RCMP training, cellblock oversight, cell access and continuous medical support.
incidents.formal_process_status: Inquest completed; six prevention recommendations issued
incidents.institutional_response: The public 2024 inquest index links the verdict but does not list a recommendation-response package for this case.
incidents.formal_outcome: The jury classified the death as accidental and made prevention recommendations. The inquest was fact-finding, not fault-finding, and did not make a finding of racism or legal responsibility.
unresolved_questions: Did the organizations addressed by the jury publish recommendation-specific responses?
Were the recommended First Nations service audit, detention standards, training, cellblock measures and continuous medical support implemented or evaluated?

incidents.title: Julian Jones inquest and remote paramedic-access recommendation
incidents.care_setting: Police wellness response and remote emergency medical access
incidents.summary: A B.C. inquest reviewed the police-involved death of Julian Jones, a Tla-o-qui-aht First Nation member, in Opitsaht. The jury recommended an Indigenous liaison for the Tofino RCMP and 24-hour water-taxi arrangements for B.C. Emergency Health Services paramedics serving the remote community.
incidents.formal_process_status: Inquest completed; four prevention recommendations issued
incidents.institutional_response: No recommendation-specific RCMP or B.C. Emergency Health Services response was located in the bounded review.
incidents.formal_outcome: The jury classified the death as homicide and made prevention recommendations. That coroner classification describes how the death occurred; it does not determine criminal or civil responsibility.
unresolved_questions: Will B.C. Emergency Health Services establish reliable round-the-clock marine transport for paramedics serving Opitsaht?
Will the Tofino RCMP establish the recommended Indigenous liaison role?

incidents.title: Anonymous Indigenous patient — rural emergency discharge review
incidents.care_setting: Rural emergency department, mental-health assessment and discharge planning
incidents.summary: A CPSBC Inquiry Committee case summary describes an Indigenous woman taken by ambulance to a rural emergency department for suicidal ideation. The committee concluded that the physician should have made greater efforts to arrange a safe trip home and documented culturally safe discharge planning.
incidents.formal_process_status: Inquiry Committee investigation concluded; regulator case summary and recommendations published
incidents.institutional_response: The physician stated that the assessment was considerate and thorough and that support options were offered. The committee identified concerns about safe discharge follow-up and documentation.
incidents.formal_outcome: This is an anonymized regulator learning summary of an Inquiry Committee review. It is not a disciplinary order, court judgment or finding about an identified hospital.
unresolved_questions: The incident date, facility and any broader institutional response are not stated publicly.
No implementation or later outcome evidence was located.

incidents.title: Anonymous Indigenous patient — reproductive-care cultural-safety review
incidents.care_setting: Reproductive health clinic and emergency follow-up care
incidents.summary: A CPSBC Inquiry Committee case summary describes an Indigenous patient who requested a support person and time to pray before a reproductive procedure. The committee was critical of the restriction on support people, comments about ceremonial needs and the lack of clear, culturally safe communication.
incidents.formal_process_status: Inquiry Committee investigation concluded; regulator case summary and recommendations published
incidents.institutional_response: The physician acknowledged the seriousness of Indigenous-specific racism and its impact on health. The clinic described its protocols, while the committee recommended stronger support-person access, communication and follow-up.
incidents.formal_outcome: This is an anonymized regulator learning summary of an Inquiry Committee review. It does not establish that the later complication was caused by the physician's conduct and is not a disciplinary order or court judgment.
unresolved_questions: The incident date, clinic and any organization-wide policy response are not stated publicly.
No implementation or later outcome evidence was located.

incidents.title: Anonymous Indigenous patient — procedure consent and pain review
incidents.care_setting: Specialist outpatient procedure
incidents.summary: A CPSBC Inquiry Committee case summary describes an Indigenous patient whose pre-procedure pain medication was missed. The committee found that the physician continued after the patient expressed pain and physically withdrew, rather than pausing to reassess needs and consent.
incidents.formal_process_status: Inquiry Committee review completed; regulator case summary published
incidents.institutional_response: The regulator reported that the physician recognized the missed medication and apologized. The committee identified consent, pain-control and culturally safe communication concerns.
incidents.formal_outcome: This is an anonymized regulator learning summary of an Inquiry Committee review. It is not a disciplinary order, court judgment or broader institutional finding.
unresolved_questions: The incident date, procedure and facility are not stated publicly.
No later remedial, institutional or implementation report was located.

incidents.title: Anonymous Indigenous patient — CPSBC professional-boundaries consent agreement
incidents.care_setting: Virtual mental-health-related medical appointment
incidents.summary: CPSBC published a consent agreement in which physician Bryan David Skrenes acknowledged crossing professional boundaries by promoting his religious beliefs and discussing his own mental-health challenges with a vulnerable Indigenous patient during a virtual appointment.
incidents.formal_process_status: Regulatory consent agreement effective September 14, 2025
incidents.institutional_response: CPSBC imposed a formal reprimand, changed the physician's registration to a disciplined class, limited workload and on-call work, and required practice restrictions and professional development.
incidents.formal_outcome: A professional-regulator consent agreement resolving the investigation. It is not a court judgment or a finding about an entire health system.
unresolved_questions: No separate public health-system response was located.
The anonymous patient's identity and private clinical details are not required for public accountability.

incidents.title: Jocelyn George inquest and custody-health recommendations
incidents.care_setting: Police custody, paramedic assessment, emergency care and air transfer
incidents.summary: A B.C. inquest reviewed the death of Jocelyn George, an Indigenous youth, after her condition deteriorated during detention in Port Alberni and she was transported to hospital and later transferred to Victoria. The verdict records that required prisoner monitoring was not consistently followed and the jury issued 24 prevention recommendations concerning health assessment, youth safety, cultural support, mental-health and addictions services, and Indigenous oversight.
incidents.formal_process_status: Inquest completed; 24 prevention recommendations issued
incidents.institutional_response: The verdict records policy and training changes after the death. A Nuu-chah-nulth Tribal Council statement said it was disappointed with the Independent Investigations Office conclusion and called for stronger custody-monitoring procedures.
incidents.formal_outcome: The jury classified the death as accidental and made prevention recommendations. The inquest did not determine criminal or civil responsibility or make a formal finding of racism.
unresolved_questions: Which recommendations received formal responses from the RCMP, City of Port Alberni, health authorities or provincial ministries?
Which recommended health, cultural-support, Indigenous-oversight or youth-wellness measures were implemented and evaluated?

incidents.title: Alyssa Josephine Talina George inquest and recommendation responses
incidents.care_setting: Police custody, emergency care, ambulance and air transfer
incidents.summary: A B.C. inquest reviewed the death of Alyssa Josephine Talina George, a First Nations woman, after she was found in medical distress in Terrace RCMP custody, taken to hospital and later transferred by air to Vancouver. The jury issued 16 prevention recommendations concerning custody monitoring, medical assessment, cultural training, laboratory practice, withdrawal-management services and information sharing.
incidents.formal_process_status: Inquest completed; 16 recommendations issued; public responses posted from six organizations
incidents.institutional_response: BCEHS, the RCMP, City of Terrace, FNHA, Ministry of Health and Terrace RCMP published responses. The responses describe policy reviews, refresher training, information-sharing practices and joint work on withdrawal-management services. These are organizational responses and claimed actions, not independent proof of implementation or outcomes.
incidents.formal_outcome: The jury classified the death as accidental and made prevention recommendations. The inquest was fact-finding, not fault-finding, and did not determine criminal or civil responsibility or make a formal finding of racism.
unresolved_questions: Which of the 16 recommendations were fully implemented and independently evaluated?
What outcomes followed the custody-health, cultural-training, information-sharing and withdrawal-management changes described by responding organizations?

incidents.title: First Nations community-care documentation and supervision consent agreement
incidents.care_setting: Home and community nursing in a First Nations community
incidents.summary: A BCCNM predecessor regulator approved a consent agreement after identifying extensive documentation, care-planning and supervision gaps in home and community nursing in a First Nations community between 2014 and 2017. The notice also describes discontinued care to an Elder based on lifestyle concerns that were not documented or corroborated.
incidents.formal_process_status: Regulatory consent agreement approved July 20, 2018
incidents.institutional_response: The regulator imposed terms equivalent to a six-month suspension, limits on in-charge and sole-nurse work, supervised practice, chart audits, and remedial education including Indigenous cultural care.
incidents.formal_outcome: A professional-regulator consent agreement concerning practice in one First Nations community. It is not a court judgment or a finding about every service provided by the organization.
unresolved_questions: The community and affected clients are not named in the public notice and are not required for accountability.
No separate public organizational response or implementation evaluation was located.

incidents.title: Discriminatory-comments nursing consent agreement
incidents.care_setting: Nursing workplace in a First Nations community
incidents.summary: BCCNM approved a consent agreement after finding that a nurse made two discriminatory and derogatory workplace comments, including one about sterilization of First Nations women, while working in a First Nations community.
incidents.formal_process_status: Regulatory consent agreement approved June 21, 2022
incidents.institutional_response: BCCNM imposed a five-week suspension, a temporary supervisory restriction, workplace mentorship, anti-racism education and sensitivity training.
incidents.formal_outcome: A professional-regulator consent agreement about specified workplace comments. It does not establish a separate patient-care event or a finding about an entire community or organization.
unresolved_questions: The public notice does not identify an affected patient or broader institutional response.
No later public implementation or workplace outcome was located.

incidents.title: Jacob George Setah inquest and youth mental-health recommendations
incidents.location: Stone Reserve, Williams Lake and Kamloops
incidents.care_setting: Rural and regional hospital care, involuntary mental-health care and police response
incidents.summary: A B.C. inquest reviewed the death of Jacob George Setah, an 18-year-old member of Yunesit’in, after he was transferred from Cariboo Memorial Hospital to Royal Inland Hospital under the Mental Health Act and left a secure ward. The jury made prevention recommendations concerning First Nations youth mental-health resources, family travel support, assessment, transfer communication, psychiatric care and hospital elopement response.
incidents.formal_process_status: Inquest completed; prevention recommendations issued; one public responder entry indexed
incidents.institutional_response: The B.C. Coroners Service response index lists an October 2017 response from the Ministry of Children and Family Development. No complete public response set or implementation ledger was located for the other organizations addressed by the jury.
incidents.formal_outcome: The jury classified the death as suicide and made prevention recommendations. The inquest was fact-finding, not fault-finding, and did not determine criminal or civil responsibility or make a formal finding of discrimination.
unresolved_questions: How did FNHA, Interior Health and the other responsible organizations respond to the recommendations?
What implementation and outcome evidence exists for youth mental-health access, family travel support, transfer communication and hospital safety measures?

incidents.title: Anonymous Indigenous patient — trauma-informed gynecology review
incidents.care_setting: Ambulatory gynecology clinic
incidents.summary: A CPSBC Inquiry Committee case summary describes an Indigenous woman seeking a first gynecological assessment who disclosed a history of sexual assault. The committee concluded that the physician did not meet expectations for culturally safe, trauma-informed care and identified missed opportunities to build trust, respond to distress and reduce re-traumatization.
incidents.formal_process_status: Inquiry Committee review completed; regulator case summary published
incidents.institutional_response: The committee considered it appropriate to end the examination for safety reasons, while finding that earlier rapport-building, clearer information and a more responsive approach could have supported a safer encounter.
incidents.formal_outcome: This is an anonymized regulator learning summary of an Inquiry Committee review. It is not a disciplinary order, court judgment or finding about an identified clinic.
unresolved_questions: The incident date, physician and clinic are not stated publicly.
No later institutional response or implementation evaluation was located.

incidents.title: Anonymous Métis patient — outpatient mental-health communication review
incidents.care_setting: Outpatient psychiatric care
incidents.summary: A CPSBC Inquiry Committee case summary describes a Métis woman who experienced a first appointment with a psychiatrist as dismissive and unsafe. The committee identified concerns about the physician's public-facing comments, tone and body language, and how the patient was asked about her Métis ancestry without a clearly documented care purpose.
incidents.formal_process_status: Inquiry Committee investigation concluded; regulator case summary and recommendations published
incidents.institutional_response: The committee issued recommendations concerning professional communication, person-led care, trauma-informed practice and culturally safe inquiry about identity.
incidents.formal_outcome: This is an anonymized regulator learning summary of an Inquiry Committee review. It is not a disciplinary order, court judgment or finding about an identified clinic.
unresolved_questions: The incident date, physician and clinic are not stated publicly.
No later institutional response or implementation evaluation was located.

incidents.title: Anonymous Indigenous patient — primary-care generalization review
incidents.care_setting: Primary care
incidents.summary: A CPSBC Inquiry Committee case summary describes an Indigenous woman who requested blood-glucose monitoring because of her family history. The committee found that the physician responded with generalized assumptions about Indigenous patients rather than a distinctions-based, patient-centred discussion, leaving the patient feeling dismissed and unsafe.
incidents.formal_process_status: Inquiry Committee review completed; regulator case summary published
incidents.institutional_response: CPSBC reported that the physician reflected on the harm, sought further education, reviewed documentation and committed to changes in practice.
incidents.formal_outcome: This is an anonymized regulator learning summary and reports a physician response within the complaint process. It is not a disciplinary order, court judgment or independent measurement of later practice change.
unresolved_questions: The incident date, physician and clinic are not stated publicly.
The public case summary does not report whether the committed practice changes were later evaluated.

incidents.title: The Silent World of Jordan — youth-custody healthcare investigation
incidents.care_setting: Youth custody, community medical clinic and emergency hospital care
incidents.summary: The Saskatchewan Advocate for Children and Youth investigated the death of a 16-year-old First Nations youth referred to publicly as Jordan. The Advocate found that the youth facility lacked adequate processes for complex needs and timely healthcare access, that signs of deteriorating health were not acted on adequately, and that the failure to accommodate Jordan's hearing impairment was improperly discriminatory and increased his disadvantage.
incidents.formal_process_status: Independent Advocate investigation completed; ten recommendations issued
incidents.institutional_response: The Advocate reported that the Ministry had conducted its own review and implemented changes. The Advocate's 2016 annual report later said the Ministry accepted all ten recommendations but required time for implementation. In 2019, a Saskatchewan Human Services Committee exchange recorded that a proposed transfer of direct correctional healthcare responsibility to the Saskatchewan Health Authority had not advanced at that time.
incidents.formal_outcome: An independent statutory Advocate investigation with findings and recommendations. The public report uses a pseudonym and does not assign criminal or civil responsibility.
unresolved_questions: What is the current recommendation-by-recommendation implementation status?
Which policy and training changes remain in operation, and what outcome evidence exists?
Was the proposed correctional-healthcare governance change completed after the 2019 committee evidence?
